newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco nearly doubles seats in future parliament.
newsitem.headline: Morocco nearly doubles seats in future parliament.

text.p: Morocco's new parliament will nearly double in size to 615 seats from 333 in the present chamber of representatives, the official MAP news agency reported on Friday.
The existing one-chamber assembly is to become a two-house parliament after legislative elections for the lower house in September.
Quoting a statement issued by the interior ministry, MAP said: "The future bi-cameral parliament will be composed of 330 seats in the Lower House and 285 in the Upper House".
The new parliament is expected to be inaugurated by King Hassan on Ocotber 10, 1997 after the legislative elections, the ministry said.
Local elections for 1,547 councils took place last month as a part of a series of elections due to culminate in September.

Under the constitution, a new Upper House is to be formed with power to topple the government through a no-confidence motion, with more than 60 percent of its members being chosen by the local councils.
The remaining third will be elected indirectly through trade unions, chambers of commerce and industry bodies before the end of September, the ministry said.
The lower house will be directly elected by universal suffrage, it added.
